title: Check PNG orientation: portrait, landscape or square

seo.metaTitle: PNG Orientation Checker - Portrait, Landscape, Square
seo.metaDescription: Find out whether an image is portrait, landscape or square, and see its pixel dimensions. Free, no upload - the file is inspected in your browser, never sent to a server.
seo.longDescription: Check PNG orientation reads the width and height of the decoded image and reports which case yours is: wider than tall is landscape, taller than wide is portrait, equal dimensions are square — together with the pixel size. It is useful before a layout decision, because a portrait screenshot and a landscape one need different containers. The check runs locally in your browser, so the file is never uploaded.
facts: Runs entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
No settings: the verdict and the pixel dimensions appear at once.
Reads the pixel dimensions, not the EXIF rotation flag of a photo.
PNG, JPG, WebP and BMP are all accepted.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
The tool reports portrait, landscape or square and shows the pixel dimensions.
Compare the reported size with the slot the image has to fit into.
If the orientation is not what you expected, use the swap orientation or rotate tools.

faq.a: By comparing width and height of the decoded image. Wider than tall is landscape, taller than wide is portrait, and any case where the two numbers are equal is square.

faq.q: Is this the same as the EXIF orientation of a photo?
faq.a: No. This tool reads the pixel dimensions of the image itself and says nothing about a camera rotation flag. A photo can be stored with a rotation flag that makes viewers display it differently from how the pixels are stored.
No. PNG, JPG, WebP and BMP are all accepted, and the answer describes the picture rather than its format.
No. The image is decoded in your browser tab; no request carries your file and nothing is stored.
